annotations.long_term_debt: Same line as total debt; Lennar files an unclassified balance sheet with no current portion, so the two rows are one figure. The blank years and quarter are filled from the segment schedules by the LEN plugin; see the total_debt annotation.
annotations.total_debt: Lennar's borrowing is a single balance-sheet line, 'Senior notes and other debts payable, net', with no current portion split out, so total debt is that line alone. FY2021-FY2023 and Q3 FY2026 tag no consolidated figure on the balance sheet -- the face prints the Homebuilding segment's line and Financial Services rides inside a lump-sum liabilities line -- so those periods are read from the operating-segments schedule, which reports the consolidated total and its segment split: FY2021 $6,378.4M, FY2022 $6,199.1M, FY2023 $4,984.0M, Q3 FY2026 $5,881.7M. Each is corroborated: every annual figure is reported identically by two 10-Ks (the year's own schedule and the next year's comparative), and Q3's total equals its own segment rows (Homebuilding $4,297.3M + Financial Services $1,584.4M). See company_plugins/LEN.py.

caveats: FY2011-FY2018 total debt stays blank. The older filings' segment schedules do not break the debt line out in the form the recent ones do, and the balance-sheet figure in those years is the Homebuilding segment alone (FY2018's $8,543.9M is Homebuilding, not the company) -- presenting it as the total would understate the debt by the Financial Services borrowing, so the honest reading is a gap.

The segment-schedule figures are read only where they corroborate themselves (segment rows summing to the printed total, or the same figure from two filings) and only into periods that are otherwise blank; an established value is never overwritten.
generated_by: session-authored from the operating-segments schedules of the FY2021-FY2025 10-Ks and the Q3 FY2026 10-Q, each figure reported by two filings or tied to its own segment rows
summary: Largest US homebuilder by revenue, with a financial services arm (mortgage origination, title, escrow) whose warehouse borrowing is a material share of the company's debt. Lennar reports November fiscal years.
